text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu slams U.N. condemnation over settlements.
- Additional 1997 budget cut will be 580 million shekels.
GLOBES
- Contacts under way to sell $150 million in Bank Leumi shares to foreign investment banks.
- Additional 1997 budget cut will be about 800 million shekels, including reduction in U.S. aid to Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Contacts under way to arrange meeting between Israeli Foreign Minister Levy and Palestinian President Arafat in Brussels next week.
- Bezeq Israel Telecom workers still on strike.
- Netanyahu and Finance Minister Neeman begin campaign to persuade cabinet ministers to support additional budget cut proposal.
- Additional 1997 budget cut could be 400 million shekels.
MAARIV
- Government will weigh in September whether to levy new taxes in 1998.
JERUSALEM POST
- Palestinian cities off-limits to Israelis.
- Court sides with Bezeq strikers.
- Army better trained for potential conflict, general says.
- Treasury: 1997 budget will exceed legal limit.
- Colombian buys 10.5 percent stake in Dankner Investments for $11.2 million.
